nutrition.review: If bodyweight has not moved after 2 full weeks of hitting these, drop 150 calories from carbs.

anchors.what: Fairlife Core Power Elite, or whey + liquid egg whites

phases.name: Re-entry
phases.note: One less set on everything. Stop 3-4 reps short. You are finding loads, not training. Everything seated or chest-supported. No hip thrust yet.

phases.name: Accumulation 1
phases.note: Full sets. Double progression: hit the top of the rep range on every set, add weight next session. Hip thrust enters week 3. Primary lifts go to 5 sets in weeks 5-6.

phases.name: Deload
phases.note: Two sets per exercise at 60% of your working weight, same reps. It will feel pointless. Do it anyway. This is what makes weeks 8-11 productive.

phases.name: Accumulation 2
phases.note: New exercises on the upper days. Primaries drop to 6-10 reps, which means heavier. Primary goes to 5 sets in weeks 10-11.

phases.name: Intensification
phases.note: Heaviest work of the block. The last set of the final accessory each day is a drop set: hit failure, strip 30%, go again to failure. One per session, no more.

phases.name: Holiday deload
phases.note: Planned light week over Christmas. Train what you can, eat what you want. This is in the program on purpose so a disrupted week does not become a lost month.

phases.name: Test
phases.note: Light on strength. Thursday is the benchmark: the exact week 3 interval session. Re-measure weight, waist and resting HR.

1: Three rounds, not four. You are re-entering. Get used to the feeling.
2: Three rounds. Last easy week before it gets real.
3: Four rounds from here. REMEMBER THIS SESSION. Week 16 repeats it exactly and you will compare.
4: Four rounds. Push from the gun, do not build into it.
5: Aim to reach 162 within 90 seconds of starting each round.
6: Same session. The adaptation is in how fast you get to target and how fast you recover.
7: DELOAD. Three rounds of three minutes, easier target. Do not be a hero.
8: Recovery drops to 2:30. Same work, less rest. This is the progression.
10: FIVE rounds. Recovery back to 3 min. Round five is the whole point.
13: FIVE minute rounds. Hardest version in the block. Minute four is where it is won.
15: Holiday deload. Do it if you can, skip it without guilt if you cannot.
16: BENCHMARK. Identical to week 3. Compare your average HR per round and how fast you recover between them.

p1.note: Primary. 30-40 degree bench. Elbows at 45 degrees, not flared.
No history here. Week 1 is finding the load.
Chest volume. Squeeze and hold a beat in the middle. Light.
SEATED with back support. Non-negotiable.
Light. Shoulder width is what makes a waist look narrow.
Elbows pinned to your sides.
Anti-rotation core. Back friendly. Slow.

p2.note: NEW. Flat bench. You have history here, and it loads heavier than incline.
NEW. Covers the upper chest angle you gave up.
NEW. Constant tension through the whole range, unlike dumbbells.
Heavier. Weeks 13-14 this is your drop set.

p1.note: Primary. Chest stays on the pad. Drive elbows back, squeeze. PER HAND.
Wide grip. Pull to the collarbone, never behind the neck.
Neutral grip. Do not rock. Torso stays still.
Rope at eye height. Posture insurance for a desk job.
No swinging.
Neutral grip hits the brachialis, which is what makes the arm look thicker.
Lower back stays flat on the floor throughout.

p2.note: NEW PRIMARY. Neutral grip, heavy. Moves to the front of the session.
NEW GRIP. Easier on the shoulder at heavier loads.
Heavier. Weeks 13-14 this is your drop set.

sat.title: Lower - Machines
sat.warmup: Lateral band walks 2 x 20 steps each direction, then glute bridges 2 x 12. Never skipped. This is the knee protection work.

p1.note: Feet mid-platform. Knees track over your second toe. Do not let the lower back round at the bottom.
WEEK 3 ONWARD. Skip entirely in weeks 1-2.
Controlled. Pause a beat at the top.
Slow on the way back.
Knee protection. Never drops out of the program.
Full stretch at the bottom, full squeeze at the top.
Bent knee hits a different calf muscle. Both variations stay in.
Squeeze glutes. Do not let the hips sag.

non_training: Two to three phone meetings a day taken walking. Most of your meetings are audio and nine hours of sitting is its own risk.
Standing desk from 20 percent to 40 percent of the day.
Ask your doctor about ApoB on the next lipid panel, and whether a calcium score fits your family history.
